reason: The picture shows the turning sensor cells at the base of a fluid-filled loop, where moving fluid bends their hairs.
expectation: This should make sensors that respond when the head starts turning.

alternatives.reason: The weights also appear to fit the tilt sensors, so that is another clear project to start.

effect: The turning sensors are complete, and the result shows how fluid movement changes their nerve signal. Next I can build the separate tilt sensors.
reaction: The fluid lag bending the sensors makes the connection clearer.
reason: The picture places the mineral weights on the jelly layer above the tilt sensor cells.
expectation: The weights and cells should form sensors that respond to tilt.

effect: The weighted sensors are complete; their shifting layer responds to tilt and changes in straight-line movement.
reaction: The picture makes the weights' role clearer.
reason: The balance nerves carry signals from both sensors to the brain, while the eye and posture routes lead from the brain and spinal cord to muscles.
expectation: This should join the incoming balance signals to routes that control eye and posture movements.

effect: The incoming and outgoing nerve routes are joined. The remaining goal is to connect them and the sensors to the body.
reaction: The arrows clarify which signals arrive and which go out.
reason: Both sensor types and the response routes are ready, but it is not yet clear which should be joined first. Inspecting the turning sensors should show their available partners.
expectation: The compatibility list should show how to connect the turning sensors to the rest of the balance system.

alternatives.reason: The routes receive signals from the sensors, but I am not sure whether the two sensor types must be joined first.

effect: The inspection automatically joined the two sensor types into balance organs. The response routes still need connecting.
reaction: It is clearer now that both sensors belong together in the inner ear.
reason: The balance response routes receive signals from the inner-ear sensors and lead toward eye and posture muscles.
expectation: This should connect the balance sensors to the routes for eye and posture movements.

effect: The balance organs cannot currently be combined with anything, so I need to find another connection first.
reaction: That was surprising because the routes seemed like a direct match.
reason: The goal is for the body to respond to head movement, so I will check how the balance response routes can connect to it.
expectation: The compatibility list should show the next available connection, possibly to the body.

effect: The routes are now connected to the body, leaving spaces for the balance sensors.
reaction: The pale spaces explain why the sensors need to be added after the routes.
reason: The balance organs fit the unconnected sensor spaces beside the ears.
expectation: The sensors should connect to the body's balance response routes, allowing it to respond to head movement.

effect: The balance organs are now connected to the body, completing the goal. The result also shows that vision and signals from muscles and joints help with balance.
reaction: It was satisfying to see the eyes turn against the head movement and the body adjust its posture.

mostWorthwhile.text: Connecting the balance organs to the body was most worthwhile: the final picture showed what the sensors and routes actually help the body do.

leastWorthwhile.text: The failed attempt to connect the organs directly to the response routes was confusing; their descriptions made them sound like a natural match.

surprise.text: I was surprised that the routes had to connect to the body before the balance organs could be added.

arbitrary.text: That required order felt a little arbitrary at first. The later picture showed the unconnected sensor spaces, but I couldn't see that prerequisite before trying.

continue.text: I would continue into another chapter: seeing the separate sensors come together in a familiar action made me curious about other body connections.
